newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Telecom reports surge in 1996 profits.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Telecom reports surge in 1996 profits.

text.p: Italian state-controlled phone company Telecom Italia, which is to be merged with its parent company Stet in preparation for sale to private investors, announced a big surge in 1996 profits on Friday.

Telecom said in a statement that net profit had jumped 53.7 percent to 2,119 billion lire ($1.26 billion) as efforts by the company to slash costs, reduce debt and develop the business fed through to the bottom line.
The company said it would pay an increased dividend of 125 lire to holders of ordinary shares and of 145 lire to savings shareholders, compared with 120 lire and 140 lire respectively in 1995.
The pay-out ratio, which measures the dividend distribution as a proportion of net profit, amounted to 49.9 percent, the statement said.

Telecom said it had slimmed down its work force in the course of 1996. Staff numbers fell by 4,192 to 86,030. but the ratio of sales turnover per individual employee rose to 333 million from 311 million lire.

The company cut its net financial indebtedness to 11,929 billion from 14,787 billion. this resulted min a fall in net fiancial charges as a proportion of turnover to 3.1 percent in 1996 from 5.1 percent.
Investments rose to 9,089 billion lire from 7,990 billion lire and were entirely financed from cash flow.

Telecom stepped up efforts to develop a wide-band network of optic fibre cable aimed at offering consumers advanced telecommunications and multimedia services. Some 600,000 dwellings had been cabled in the course of the year, the statement said.

Domestic phone traffic rose by 6.3 percent over 1995 while international phone traffic jumped 12.3 percent over the same period. Telecom had launched two internet access services which had taken on 95,000 subscribers.

Telecom was also working on a new cordless telephone service. The company, which had successfully tested the service in late 1996, was awaiting authorisation from the Post and Telecommunications Ministry.

The company said that investments totalling 26 trillion lire in three years had allowed Telecom to reach a level of technological sophistication which put it on an equal footing with other telecoms operators. $=1,687
